# BB00227: Du'a' li'n-Nuri'l-Ahmar {.unnumbered}

In Thy Book, through every prayer that Thou hast fashioned or that hath been uttered about Thee, for all grace belongeth unto Thee, resideth in Thee, emanateth from Thee, and returneth unto Thee, and there is no power nor strength except through Thee, and unto Thee is the final return. This is a prayer to the crimson light whose bearer was Israfil, peace be upon him:

In the Name of God, the Exalted, the Most Holy

O my God! I beseech Thee by the most magnificent of Thy Divinity, though all Thy Divinity is magnificent with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Divinity.

O my God! I beseech Thee by the most impregnable of Thy Loftiness, though all Thy Loftiness is impregnable with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Loftiness.

O my God! I beseech Thee by the most glorious of Thy Might, though all Thy Might is glorious with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Might.

O my God! I beseech Thee by the most enduring of Thy Eternity, though all Thy Eternity is enduring with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Eternity.

O my God! I beseech Thee by the most guiding of Thy Guidance, though all Thy Guidance is guiding with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Guidance.

O my God! I beseech Thee by the most resplendent of Thy Oneness, though all Thy Oneness is resplendent with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Oneness.

O my God! I beseech Thee by the most pure of Thy Purity, though all Thy Purity is pure with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Purity.

O my God! I beseech Thee by the most lasting of Thy Life, though all Thy Life is lasting with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Life.

O my God! I beseech Thee by the most sanctified of Thy Sanctity, though all Thy Sanctity is sanctified with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Sanctity.

O my God! I beseech Thee by the most steadfast of Thy Certitude, though all Thy Certitude is steadfast with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Certitude.

O my God! I beseech Thee by the most cooling of Thy Camphor, though all Thy Camphor is cooling with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Camphor.

O my God! I beseech Thee by the most subtle of Thy Grace, though all Thy Grace is subtle with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Grace.

O my God! I beseech Thee by the most excellent of Thy Dominion, though all Thy Dominion is excellent with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Dominion.

O my God! I beseech Thee by the most luminous of Thy Light, though all Thy Light is luminous with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Light.

O my God! I beseech Thee by the most sovereign of Thy Sovereignty, though all Thy Sovereignty is sovereign with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Sovereignty.

O my God! I beseech Thee by the most transcendent of Thy Transcendence, though all Thy Transcendence is transcendent with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Transcendence.

O my God! I beseech Thee by the most singular of Thy Singleness, though all Thy Singleness is singular with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Singleness.

O my God! I beseech Thee by the most hallowed of Thy Self-Subsistence, though all Thy Self-Subsistence is hallowed with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Self-Subsistence.

O my God! I beseech Thee by the most enduring of Thy Everlastingness, though all Thy Everlastingness is enduring with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Everlastingness.

O my God! I beseech Thee by the most embracing of Thy Mercy, though all Thy Mercy is embracing with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Mercy.

O my God! I beseech Thee by the most exalted of Thy Gratitude, though all Thy Gratitude is exalted with Thee, then in the Mother Book, O my God! I beseech Thee by all Thy Gratitude.

O God! I beseech Thee by the swiftest of Thy repentances, and all Thy repentances are swift with Thee and then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy repentances.

O God! I beseech Thee by the most steadfast of Thy steadfastness, and all Thy steadfastness is steadfast with Thee and then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy steadfastness.

O God! I beseech Thee by the most encompassing of Thy treasuries, and all Thy treasuries are encompassing with Thee and then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy treasuries.

O God! I beseech Thee by the mightiest of Thy offspring, and all Thy offspring are mighty with Thee and then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy offspring.

O God! I beseech Thee by the most luminous of Thy light, and all Thy light is luminous with Thee and then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy light.

O God! I beseech Thee by the most manifest of Thy manifestation, and all Thy manifestation is manifest with Thee and then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy manifestation.

O God! I beseech Thee by the most enriching of Thy riches, and all Thy riches are abundance with Thee and then in the Mother Book. O God! I beseech Thee by all Thy riches.

O God! I beseech Thee by Thyself—there is none beside Thee equal, comparable, similar, like or resembling Thee—and by that which Thou hast loved for Thyself or lovest through the sublimity of Thy inaccessibility and the exaltation of Thy transcendence. For all things, O my God, bow down before Thy Countenance and are humble before Thine eyes. Thou art unique in Thy unity above all contingent beings, singular in the sovereignty of Thy eternity above all existing things, supreme in the dominion of Thy self-subsistence above all created things, and exalted in the inaccessible heights of Thine everlasting nature above all that is still or in motion. Thou art independent in the independence of Thy sanctity above all who dwell in the kingdoms of earth and heaven, sovereign in the sovereignty of Thy glory above all who inhabit the realms of names and attributes. Thou hast taken possession, through the dominion of Thy beloved nature, of all that Thou hast loved in the depths of names and attributes, and art magnificent in the majesty of Thy glory as the Object of all desire, above all that can be mentioned through similitude or allusion.

Thou art the Exalted One before Whose exaltation all bow down in humility, and the Attributed One before Whose transcendence all stand in reverence. All glorify Thee, proclaim Thy unity, magnify Thee and extol Thee according to their capacity. But perchance there may be directed toward Thee that which Thou hast foreordained of pure, crystalline, essential and abstract realities, and that by which Thou art remembered in the kingdom of names and attributes. There is no hour which Thou hast not made great, majestic, beautiful, mighty and illumined with the light that quivers from the Dayspring of morning and shines forth from the holy Star.

We shall assuredly cause to descend, O God, Thy light upon the Tree of Oneness and that which Thy knowledge hath encompassed therein, as befits the sublimity of Thy generosity, the exaltation of Thy grace, the elevation of Thy bounty, the inaccessibility of Thy tenderness and the independence of Thy loving-kindness; and upon all save the Tree of Thy love that which it deserves before Thy justice, the sovereignty of Thy omnipotence, Thy power, the dominion of Thy might, Thy glory and the court of Thy supreme grandeur. For Thy mercy transcends all mercy, Thy severity all severity, Thy might all might, Thy sovereignty all sovereignty, Thy grandeur all grandeur, and Thy power all power. Grant us, O God, that which we deserve, and pardon us, O God, through Thy grace and bounty for that which we deserve not before the independence of the sovereignty of Thy oneness and the majesty of the dominion of Thy eternity. Verily, Thou art the Self-Sufficient, the Most Exalted, the All-Forgiving, the Inaccessible, possessed of might and majesty.

Bless, O God, the bearer of Thy crimson light, Israfil, peace be upon him, morning and evening.
